correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the three Laplacian invariant subspaces (leaf differences, clique differences, three-class quotient), giving gap min{c,a+(n-1)b,mu_-}. Concavity and orbit averaging cover arbitrary nonnegative asymmetric competitors. Unit-gap normalization yields a strict convex G(a) with derivative n/2-m^2(n-1)/((n+m)a-(m+1))^2 and unique threshold m=sqrt(n(n-1)/2). The optimal conductances meet every eigenvalue constraint; the all-optima zero-support claim follows from nonnegative orbit averaging; the opposite direction follows from the strictly inferior star-only budget. Included verify.py passed 1,779 matrix, cost, spectrum, threshold and nonsymmetric-sample checks, which are supplementary to the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The exact arbitrary-conductance pineapple optimum and its threshold m=sqrt(n(n-1)/2) are not stated or obtained as graph-family corollaries by the inspected primary works. Sun et al. give a general semidefinite formulation and cases for paths/cycles; Ghosh–Boyd give convex and symmetry bounds; Topcu–Sorgun–Haemers study the adjacency spectrum and cospectrality of pineapple graphs rather than optimized Laplacian eigenvalues. Available closely related network-design claims have different attachment patterns. Searches and comparisons cannot prove novelty; specialized prior coverage remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The pineapple graph is a standard natural coalescence of a complete graph and star. Its fixed-budget optimal mixing design has a previously nonobvious competition between clique reinforcement and terminal servicing. The exact two-parameter cutoff m=sqrt(n(n-1)/2) decides when every optimizer discards an entire edge orbit. It provides a globally valid analytical design rule and avoids solving a semidefinite program for each (n,m).
